name: hero-view-timeline
title: Hero view timeline
author: Eduardo Retana
description: A hero that names its view-timeline; the headline splits apart while the hero leaves. It never animates in, so the LCP paints at full opacity. Pure CSS.

meta.descriptionEs: Hero que nombra su view-timeline; el titular se abre hacia los lados mientras el hero sale. Nunca entra animado, así el LCP pinta completo. CSS puro.
meta.usage: <HeroViewTimeline title="Vajillas por encargo hechas a mano" lead={lead} actions={<Button>Agenda una visita</Button>} />

api.name: title / eyebrow / lead / actions
api.description: The title splits at its middle word. Actions are the host's own buttons or links.

api.name: headingAs / range
api.description: Default h1 (the page's only h1). Exit range on the hero's timeline, default exit 0% exit 70%.

api.name: loading / error / labels / motion
api.description: Skeleton, alert in place of the actions, copy, and a still mode.

docs: Idea from Midudev's scroll-driven animations demo (reel, 2026). Technical reference: MDN, CSS scroll-driven animations. Implementation is Retana UI's own; no code from the reel. Pure CSS with a local <style>: no JavaScript, no client boundary, safe in a Server Component. The animation sits inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and @supports (animation-timeline: …), and animation-timeline comes after the animation shorthand. Without support or with reduced motion the content is visible and still. Pass motion="off" to hold it still from a toggle. Baseline 2026 newly available (27 Oct 2026): Chrome and Edge 115+, Safari 26+, Firefox 159+. The item ships no theme, cssVars, or fixed colors. Loading and error are host states: the piece renders a skeleton or an alert. The section declares view-timeline: --retana-hero block; the halves and the lead animate translate on the exit range only; text stays at full opacity so it keeps AA contrast while it moves.
